key_insight: HP-RLVR assigns token-level credit from a single completed rollout by comparing each token under its normal causal context versus a hindsight context that includes the realized future and verifier feedback.
engineering_relevance: It removes the need for group sampling, reference solutions, or a learned critic, making RLVR training more sample-efficient and practical for long-horizon reasoning tasks.
method: Score each eligible token under two views: causal history and hindsight context.
Compute a normalized Jensen–Shannon divergence between the two scores to produce bounded token credit.
Use this hindsight-weighted signal to update the policy from one rollout per prompt.
evidence_signal: On paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared 100-step schedule, HP-RLVR trained 1.21×, 1.46×, and 2.30× faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld using one-eighth the rollouts per prompt.
watch_item: Because the method depends on hindsight-conditioned token scoring from the generating policy snapshot, careful implementation is needed to avoid unstable credit assignment or leakage from verifier feedback.
paper_title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
